title: Selector Lab: select elements and see matched rules
learningObjectives: Explain selector lab: select elements and see matched rules and design an accessible interactive learning lab.

understand.concept: A Selector Lab lets learners choose or edit a CSS selector and see which sample elements match. It can display matched element labels and the computed styles affected by the rule. The selector input must be handled safely and invalid selectors must produce a helpful error.
understand.whyItMatters: The lab teaches selector matching without injecting user text into HTML. Use querySelectorAll inside a controlled preview document, catch selector syntax errors, and keep the sample markup isolated from the parent application.
understand.analogy: The lab is a search tool: the selector is the query and highlighted sample elements are the matches.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports understanding; a production lab needs real state management, safe preview isolation, and accessible controls.

explain.narrative: The two .note elements receive the sample style. The full interactive selector editor is the independent build task.

practise.guidedTask: Build a selector input that validates with querySelectorAll, highlights matching preview elements, lists the matches, and catches invalid selector errors without using innerHTML.
practise.independentTask: Implement the lab with labelled controls, a live preview, validation, reset behaviour, and a generated CSS readout. Test keyboard and mobile operation.
hints: Keep preview state and code output synchronized.
Handle invalid input without crashing the lab.
Keep learner content isolated from the parent application.
